title: Range translation does not run when the first series is added
description: The effect depends on `range` and `mount.ready`, but `seriesCountRef` is updated by facade calls without triggering a render. If a series is added while the range is unchanged, this effect never applies the current range; removing and re-adding a series has the same issue. The translation tests only exercise adding a series followed by changing the range, which triggers the effect and misses this case. Add a reactive series-count signal or otherwise trigger translation when series membership changes.

title: Adding data does not activate range synchronization
description: After the hook becomes ready, adding the first populated series only updates a ref. None of the effect dependencies change, so the existing Context range remains unapplied until another range change occurs. The translation test masks this by calling `setRange` immediately after `addSeries`. Make data availability reactive and test adding data without changing the range.

title: Series count does not establish data availability
description: `addSeries` increments the count even for valid `data: []` configurations, and `updateSeries` can clear all data without updating that count. Consequently, the hook’s empty-time-scale guard permits `setVisibleRange` when no points exist—the failure it explicitly intends to prevent. Track populated series across additions, updates, and removals; cover empty-series and data-clearing cases.

title: Applying the current range is not triggered when a series is added
description: The range effect only reruns when `mount.ready`, `chart`, or `range` changes. Adding a series updates `seriesCountRef` in `src/chart/chart-facade.ts:49-55`, but changing a ref does not rerun the effect. As a result, a chart that becomes populated after mount does not receive the current range unless the range changes later. The translation test changes the range after adding a series, so it does not cover this case.

title: Later operation failures overwrite the documented first error
description: `setOperationError` replaces `current.error` on every failure. This conflicts with the `UseChartProviderResult` contract in `src/chart/chart-operations.ts:77`, which says `error` is the first error. A second failed operation therefore changes the reported error instead of preserving the first.

title: Adding the first series does not retrigger visible-range translation
description:
The effect depends only on `mount.ready`, `chart`, and `range`, while series presence is tracked by mutating `seriesCountRef.current` in `buildChartOperations.addSeries`. A successful `addSeries` does not update React state or otherwise invalidate the effect. Consequently, if the range changes while the chart is empty and a series is added later—the expected asynchronous-data flow—the effect has already run and skipped the range, and it will not run again. The current range is therefore never sent to the provider.

The `applies the range once a series exists` test in `src/test/use-chart-provider.translation.test.tsx` masks this by changing the range only after adding the series. Promote series readiness or a series revision into React state and include it in the effect dependencies, or explicitly apply the current range after a successful first-series addition. Add a regression test with the reverse ordering: range first, series second.

title: Later failures replace the documented first error
description: `setOperationError` unconditionally assigns the latest failure, although the public contract in `src/chart/chart-operations.ts:77` says `error` contains the “first error from any provider operation.” If two operations fail, the second masks the original diagnostic. Preserve the existing error with `current.error ?? failure`, or change the public contract if the latest-error behavior is intentional. The existing test only verifies that a later successful operation does not clear the error; it should force two failures and verify the required behavior.

title: Mount-stage failures are always logged as create failures
description: The catch covers the entire mount sequence, including initial resize, `ResizeObserver` construction and observation, and both subscription registrations. Nevertheless, every failure is logged as `provider create failed`, which can send developers toward the wrong stage. Log a generic `provider mount failed` message or introduce stage-specific errors for create, resize, observer setup, and subscription setup.

title: Exported React components omit explicit return types
description: The TypeScript convention requires explicit return types on exported functions, but `ChartRoute` has none. The same issue exists in `src/app/App.tsx#App` and `src/routes/routes.tsx#RootLayout`. Add explicit `ReactElement` or equivalent return annotations to these exported components.
